correctness.rationale: Dekking–van Loon Theorem 4.4 identifies natural base-φ count V(N) with R(F_{r+2}N). The new tail-shift by two Zeckendorf positions gives R(F_{r+4}N) whose block recursion has C0=R(F4)=2 and C1=R(F_{s1+5}+3)=s1+2 (from the F_j+3 decomposition); the same published gap recurrence matrices and initial sums K0+V0, K1+V1 imply C=K+V by induction. Published Knott-vs-natural difference recursion has D0=0 and D1=0 or 1 by least gap parity; positive-gap matrices propagate D>0 exactly when its last gap is odd. Proposition 5.1 identifies precisely the even vs odd Lucas intervals. Lucas boundary K=2j+1,V=1 gives unbounded ratio. Source verifier partitions exact finite integer cases but is not an infinite proof.
residual_risks: The result depends on the standard Fibonacci binary-flip block recursion; earlier Robbins/Klarner versions may contain equivalent unindexed count identities.
